Something I always try to stress, both here and with the new band, is that it's truly an honor. In this case, nobody's paying money - but they're still paying time and attention. You're still paying effort and are working. With a band, people are paying good money to hear what we can do. For just a little while, they let us control their emotions. They give me permission to remind them of times long since past and make new memories.

That's such an honor. It really is. In all but the rarest of cases, the audience is way too good to us. There's a moment when you look out and, through the lights, you can see someone with tears in their eyes. Sometimes, you can hear them laugh. It's great when they sing in time. It's even more awesome when they are all wiggling and everyone just happens to get it right - even if just for a few minutes.

I get to give them that. I get to take that from them - their control. I have the mic, or at least a mic. I enable them to forget about their issues and live in the moment. I give healing, sometimes. I've had so many people express how they managed to get over something because of a song we played. I also have had so many folks just happy to hear someone play it like they remembered - and not with any twists.

There's some great benefits to doing covers and faithful replication. It really is a great honor to be able to do that. I'd do it for free, if I could. Hell, I have. But, I need the kids to make a living. So, I'll make sure we're paid and paid well. I've got four gigs lined up and I'm looking at two hall rentals and maybe, just maybe, doing a big show at the Augusta Civic Center.

I used to be pretty scared on the stage. I'd hide in the shadows, not face the audience much, and never even considered singing. Eventually, that grows old and you start to turn around and look out into the audience.

You can see them dance, laugh, sing, drink, smoke, flirt, and more. For all the watching they do, you're just as much looking into their lives.

What I like is there occasion where you meet someone's eyes for a brief moment and you can tell that the song is meaningful. So, for just a moment, you throw yourself into the music even harder. You'll throw in a little flourishing and make it fancy - and you're playing just for them, as far as they're concerned.

Indeed, you are playing just for them - just for that briefest of moments. A good song for that is Lightning Crashes. That'll get some tears flowing sometimes. Cats In The Cradle is another good one.

Sometimes, you'll notice someone's having a hard time - so you'll go from that song into one that's a little further down the list and put something up-beat and happy in there.

I'm so very excited to be going back out to play for a while longer. It's a lot of work, but I truly love the job.

It’s really so meaningful to be able to touch the hearts of people. I pray your new adventure is life changing in a absolute beautifully blessed way!
